# Life cycle assessment
What is the impact on the life cycle assessment of the work or project such as the CO2 footprint? 

- Describe the life cycle of your product or service.

- For all the phases of the life cycle of your product or service assess their impact. You can use the CO2 footprint calculation data provided in the lecture and in the paper mentioned in the lecture about PCB footprint if it is relevant to your project. Website about sustainable software design, [here](https://leobit.com/blog/why-sustainable-software-engineering-matters/)

- Add the assessed impact of all the different phases to capture the overall impact of the work or project.

## The PCF value 
The PCF value is measured by quantifying the GHG emissions for the entire product life cycle expressed in carbon dioxide equivalents value (kg CO2 eq.), as per ISO/TS 14067. 

**CFtotal = CFRM + CFM + CFD + CFU + CFEOL** 

• CFRM is the carbon footprint of the raw material stage (kg CO2 eq.); 

• CFM is the carbon footprint of the manufacturing stage (kg CO2 eq.); 

• CFD is the carbon footprint of the distribution stage (kg CO2 eq.); 

• CFU is the carbon footprint of the use stage (kg CO2 eq.); 

• CFEOL is the carbon footprint of the end-of-life stage (kg CO2 eq.) (International Organization for Standardization (ISO), 2013).

## Software dev sustainability :
### **Resource efficiency and optimisation**
- Sustainable software should achieve maximum functionality while consuming minimum resources.

- Unnecessary features, inefficient algorithms and excessive data processing increase energy consumption.

- Removing redundant functions and optimising data storage and transfer can reduce the resources required to operate software.

- Measuring environmental performance helps identify areas where improvements are needed.

#1. Carbon

[Training a single AI model](https://www.technologyreview.com/2019/06/06/239031/training-a-single-ai-model-can-emit-as-much-carbon-as-five-cars-in-their-lifetimes/) emits as much carbon as five cars in their lifetime. A [recent study](https://arxiv.org/ftp/arxiv/papers/2104/2104.10350.pdf) found that training GPT-3, with its 175 billion parameters, consumed 1,287 MWh of electricity and produced 502 metric tons of carbon emissions. This is comparable to the emissions generated by 112 gasoline-powered cars over the course of a year. So make sure every gram of carbon emitted due to software system use brings the maximum value.

#2. Energy

We burn fossil fuels to produce the most electricity. Therefore, energy consumed by devices and hardware is never clean. The cost of powering a data center comprises a significant share of its annual operating budget. This means that optimization of electricity use should be one of the sustainable software priorities.

#3. Carbon intensity

Aim for the zero-carbon intensity of electricity (emissions per kilowatt-hour of consumed electricity). It mostly depends on your location and the type of power used with devices. Hydroelectric plants have cleaner energy than mixed electricity sources.

#4. Embodied carbon

Embodied carbon is the result of hardware production and disposal. The more efficiently you use hardware, the less carbon it generates in the long run.

#5. Energy proportionality

Energy proportionality software development principles mean that the power a computer system consumes must translate to real work. The more someone uses a computer, the more efficiently it converts electricity into value.

#6. Network efficiency

When software sends data online, it uses many devices in the network, each of which consumes electricity and causes carbon emissions. That’s why tech companies should reduce the size of data and hops between network devices, the distance data travels, and make network devices more energy-efficient.

#7. Demand shaping

Align your electricity demand with the existing supply for sustainable programming. When the renewable energy supply is high, maximize the use of applications. When demand is low, use them less.

#8. Optimization

The last of the green software development principles states that there are many ways to reduce the environmental impact of ICT. The key sustainable programming point is to choose the measurement criterion that clearly shows where to channel optimization efforts. Apart from the listed sustainable software development principles, you should use human resources efficiently. It’s crucial to optimize the work of your tech team and adopt an optimum pace. It will allow you to continuously improve your product instead of making hasty decisions to meet deadlines.
